title: The Door
text: A venue checks ages at the door with a phone app. Requests go to the customer's wallet, and proofs come back.
held: One fact was asked for, one fact was given, and it was good for tonight only.

cards.label: Decline the request
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: asks for
fields.check: Read what the request really asks for

intrusion.value: name, address and date of birth
intrusion.detail: The request asks for the full identity, not a fact.
intrusion.why: A verifier that asks for everything isn't doing an age check. The wallet's job is to notice.
intrusion.reveal: The venue's request asked for the customer's full identity.

cards.label: Reject the proof
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: made for
fields.check: Check the nonce in the proof
fields.ok: It carries the nonce you sent a moment ago.

intrusion.detail: The nonce is not one you sent tonight.
intrusion.why: Someone is showing a proof that was made for somebody else's visit.
intrusion.reveal: The proof carried the nonce of a different night's request.

temptations.label: Photograph the customer's screen for the records
temptations.why: A photo of a proof is a copy of a proof, which is what the nonce exists to make useless. And it is one more thing to leak.

teaches: Wallets should refuse requests that ask for more than the purpose needs.
Verifiers should refuse proofs that weren't made for them, now.

question.text: Before play: what should the venue learn about a customer?
question.why: Everything beyond the one fact is a liability for the venue and a loss for the customer.

options.label: That they are over 18, and nothing else
Their name and date of birth
